topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Consider a rectangle with sides f(x) and g(x).
Visualize the rectangle area as f(x) times g(x).
animations: Display power rule x^n in white #FFFFFF.
Show with height f(x) and width g(x) in blue #3498DB.
Fade in area label A = f(x)g(x) in light green #2ECC71.

sections.title: The Product Rule (0:45-2:00)
lecture_lines: The Product Rule finds the derivative of f(x)g(x).
Visualize changes as adding rectangle strips.
animations: Show product rule formula in white #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Transitioning to Nested Functions (2:00-2:30)
lecture_lines: Some functions contain other functions inside.
We call these nested or composite functions.
Think of layers like a Russian doll.
animations: Show f(x) and g(x) nested as f(g(x)) in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight inner function g(x) with light blue #5DADE2 border.
Animate nested layers stacking like Russian dolls in purple #AF7AC5 using.

sections.title: The Chain Rule (2:30-4:15)
lecture_lines: Chain Rule differentiates composite functions f(g(x)).
Multiply outer derivative by inner derivative.
Visualize gear ratios for change propagation.
See how inner change affects outer change.
animations: Display Chain Rule d/dx f(g(x)) in white #FFFFFF.
Show multiplier structure f'(g(x)) and g'(x) in orange #F39C12.
Highlight outer derivative f'(g(x)) in red #E74C3C.
Highlight inner derivative g'(x) in green #2ECC71.
Visualize inner and outer gears spinning in yellow #F1C40F using.

sections.title: Synthesis & Summary (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: Solve problems needing both Product and Chain Rules.
Identify the primary rule skeleton first.
Use Chain Rule for inner components.
Differentiate outside while keeping inside fixed.
Finally multiply by the inner derivative.
animations: Display combined f'(x)g(x) + f(x)g'(x) and f'(g(x))g'(x) in white #FFFFFF.
Highlight core skeleton of derivative rules in orange #F39C12.
Highlight inner component using Chain Rule in green #2ECC71.
Animate step-by-step simplification of complex functions in light gray #BDC3C7.
Show final multiplication step by flashing white #FFFFFF.
